author: t. j. gough
title: Zsombor Velcz reflects on journey from Hungary to Baylor tennis team
text:
Zsombor Velcz, a senior on the Baylor men’s tennis team, described his experience adjusting to life in the United States and becoming part of the Baylor community in remarks shared on Apr. 15. Originally from Budapest, Hungary, Velcz enrolled at Baylor as a freshman in 2022 and faced both cultural and athletic transitions.
Velcz said that moving from an individual sport background to joining a college team was a significant change. “Tennis is an individual sport,” he said. “I didn’t really understand until I got here how it feels to be part of a team and play for something bigger than yourself.” He explained that his time at Baylor has helped him understand not only the game but also life more broadly.
Baylor coach Michael Woodson highlighted Velcz’s growth since arriving at the university. “From the moment Zsombor arrived in the fall of 2022, we believed in who he could become,” Woodson said. “But what he’s done here has meant so much more than just his development as a player. Baylor has truly become a second home for him, and the relationships he’s built with his teammates, our staff and the community are a big part of that. He’s not just part of this program – he’s family.” The sense of unity within the team was especially apparent after teammate Devin Badenhorst experienced personal tragedy during their sophomore year.
Velcz recounted his own path to college tennis after winning national titles in Hungary and competing internationally during a gap year following high school graduation. He cited education as an important factor in choosing Baylor: “Student-athlete is not a thing in Hungary. Here, I can study and play tennis at the same time. That was a huge perk for me and made my decision much easier,” he said.
Reflecting on lessons learned early at Baylor about representing his school, Velcz recalled advice from associate head coach Izak van der Merwe about wearing college gear with pride: “There is so much weight you carry when you play in Baylor gear representing Baylor… It’s a great honor for me to play for Baylor and represent the school.” Over three seasons with All-Big 12 honors each year, Velcz has contributed significantly to his team’s success.
Looking ahead to graduation this August with degrees across several disciplines, Velcz remains undecided about pursuing further studies but plans to begin playing professionally after taking some time off post-season. Woodson praised him by saying: “He’s grown into a confident, complete player on the court through his work ethic and competitiveness… He represents Baylor the right way every day, and we’re incredibly proud of the young man he’s become.”
